text.p: Defending men's champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov followed his female counterpart Steffi Graf out of the French Open on Tuesday when he was beaten 6-2 5-7 2-6 6-0 6-4 by Brazil's Gustavo Kuerten in the quarter-finals.
Kuerten, ranked 66th in the world, will now meet another rank outsider, Filip Dewulf of Belgium, in the semifinals at Roland Garros.

Kafelnikov, who missed three months' tennis earlier this year after breaking a finger in training before the Australian Open in January, had looked in prime form in his previous round against Australian Mark Philippoussis.
But the Russian world number three was unable to rediscover anything like the same touch against his eager 20-year-old opponent, playing in only his second grand slam tournament.

Kuerten's agility around the baseline allowed him to claw his way back from two sets to one down and he permitted his opponent just eight points during an extraordinary fourth set in which Kafelnikov failed to win a game.
The Brazilian, who ignored pre-match requests from organisers to abandon his blue and yellow kit for a more traditional ensemble, finally wrapped up victory in two and a half hours.
